notes: Session provenance: this is a brand-new independent review session. This session did not implement T3 and did not take part in any earlier review of T3. Reading the earlier review was used to identify the regression to verify, not as verification evidence.

P2 resolved: captions.py:64-68 places the exclusive whole-second final bound strictly after every cue start, including terminal missing/null/zero durations. captions.py:50 assigns nonnegative-start cues by half-open intervals; every tested cue appears exactly once in fixed, embedding, and single modes. Boundary tests include 0s, 20s windows, 45s minimum, 90s fixed cuts, a selected 120s semantic cut, 180s, 300s, 3600s, and fractional neighbors. The prior three-cue IndexError reproducer now returns one embedding segment [0,181) containing all three cues.

Index safety: captions.py:91-92 excludes candidates at or outside the outer bounds before indexing both neighbors. Recursive splitting also requires a strictly internal boundary at lines 103-105. No IndexError occurred in edge or randomized probes.

Determinism: windows and candidate boundaries are sorted; equal depths break toward earlier times at captions.py:90 and :108. Competing equal-depth boundaries at 100/160/220s with min_s=90 yield [0,100), [100,220), [220,320), identical including text across repeats and PYTHONHASHSEED 0,1,42,999.

Length semantics follow the specified algorithm: semantic cuts require min_s on both sides; segments longer than max_s are recursively split or use fixed_s. With default settings and tested valid custom settings (fixed_s <= max_s), nonsingle segments stayed within max_s. Fixed splitting may leave a final tail shorter than min_s, and fewer than two windows deliberately returns single even for a long cue. Thus min_s/max_s are not unconditional bounds across all modes. These exceptions match Task T3 and design 3.1, rather than constituting new must-fix defects.

Fallback verified against the exact None-embedder result for exceptions, None/scalar/empty/ragged/nonnumeric results, wrong row count, wrong rank, zero columns, NaN, positive/negative infinity, all-zero embeddings and a single zero-norm row. All yield fixed mode when the single-mode precondition does not apply.

Performance: 3600s inputs contain 180 windows with either 720 or 3600 cues. Forty runs per case cover constant, structured, and 1024-dimensional random embeddings. Median times range from 1.376 to 6.695ms; largest observed run is 7.866ms. This measures local segmentation with fake/precomputed embeddings, not remote embedding latency. Quadratic depth scans and cue scans are small at this configured duration/window size.

Tests are meaningful: exact segment locations and content, parsing/filtering/sorting, minimum semantic length, forced fixed splitting, malformed embedding fallback, fractional boundary assignment, and nine missing/null/zero-duration regression cases are asserted. Independent old-source reproduction confirms the regression cases distinguish the broken behavior. Committed tests do not explicitly lock cross-process ties, one-hour performance, or zero-duration single mode; independent temporary probes cover those gaps. No must-fix test deficiency found.

Scope: normal JSON3 nonnegative cue times and positive segmentation parameters. Repository source, tests, index, and Git refs were not modified. Probe scripts and output were written under TMPDIR; the only repository file created is this requested review JSON.
